sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: face_recognition is a Python library and command-line tool that finds faces in photos, locates facial features like eyes and mouth, and recognises who is in a picture by comparing it with photos of people you know.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building face detection and recognition from scratch needs deep learning expertise. This library wraps dlib's face recognition model, which the README says scores 99.38% on the Labeled Faces in the Wild benchmark, behind a few simple function calls.
whoFor: Python developers adding face detection to an app
Hobbyists building photo or camera projects
People sorting photo collections by person
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the simplest possible face recognition API in Python. Be aware of its caveats: it works less well on children and accuracy may vary between ethnic groups.
requirements: macOS or Linux (Windows not officially supported)

overview: face_recognition is built on dlib's deep learning face recognition model. From Python you can find all faces in an image, get the outline of each person's eyes, nose, mouth and chin, and compare face encodings to decide whether two photos show the same person.

Installing it also gives you two command-line tools. face_recognition takes a folder with one photo of each known person, named after them, and a folder of unknown photos, and prints who appears in each. face_detection prints the pixel coordinates of every face it finds.

An optional CNN face detector is more accurate but needs an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA for good performance. Because dlib is written in C++, deploying to cloud hosts can be tricky, so the repository includes a Dockerfile and docker-compose setup.

troubleshooting.solution: Install dlib with Python bindings and cmake first, or use the Docker image or the pre-configured VM the README links.

troubleshooting.problem: The same person matches several names

troubleshooting.solution: The model is trained on adults and doesn't work well on children at the default threshold.
It needs an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA and dlib compiled with CUDA support.
Check the Common Errors page in the project wiki.
